channel.title: Worcester Business Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Worcester Business Journal (wbjournal.com)

item.title: Lifeward regains Nasdaq compliance following reverse stock split
item.description: Medical device manufacturer Lifeward in Marlborough has regained compliance with Nasdaq listing requirements a month after receiving notice it risked delisting.

item.title: Ameresco completes $30M Army geothermal project
item.description: The Framingham-based firm replaced traditional HVAC systems with American-manufactured, ground-source heat pumps.

item.title: 🔒 Marlborough AI firm acquires London’s Candyspace
item.description: Quantiphi, a Marlborough-based artificial intelligence consulting and engineering firm, has acquired Candyspace, a digital platform designer out of London.

item.title: Economic development, environmental projects land $4.8M in federal funding
item.description: The funding is part of $12.1 million allocated to projects in Congressman Jim McGovern’s (D-Worcester) district.

item.title: Cannabis regulators vote to continue limiting delivery licenses to social equity businesses
item.description: The vote came as the original exclusivity period was set to expire April 1.

item.title: Economic development bill still work in progress as Healey highlights business expansions
item.description: "We have some strengths that other states would kill for and we also have our challenges," the governor said.

item.title: O’Connor’s Restaurant & Bar closing for good after 37 years of operation
item.description: Just ahead of the St. Patrick’s Day holiday, O’Connor’s Restaurant & Bar is closing for good.

item.title: UMass Chan receives $800K for ALS research
item.description: The Angel Fund for ALS Research, based in Wakefield, awarded UMass Chan $800,000 to fund the research of Dr. Robert Brown and Daryl Bosco.

item.title: QCC joins statewide apprenticeship degree program
item.description: Through the initiative, QCC students will simultaneously enroll in class for credit while participating in paid apprenticeships.

item.title: 🔒 Country Bank adds Stepalavich as chief technology officer
item.description: Stepalavich began his career offering computer repair and technology services to local businesses before moving to multiple roles in the healthcare and banking sectors.
